issues.failure_explanation: With δ = ε = N^{−1/(n+2)}, the additive term in (T2_1) is 6N^{−1/(n+2)}, which exceeds the claimed O(D²log²D N^{−2/(n+2)}log⁴N) by a factor N^{1/(n+2)}; the covering term is of order N^{−2/(n+2)}polylog and cannot absorb it, so (T2_11) does not follow from (T2_1). The same leftover affects (T2_2) and (T2_3). The rate itself is recoverable by choosing the free parameter δ at the order of the target rate (δ ≍ N^{−2/(n+2)} up to log factors), which at most doubles the log(δ^{−1}) factors inside the covering bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: choose the free deviation parameter δ of order N^{−2/(n+2)} (up to log factors) instead of δ = ε and redo the covering-number substitution; the covering term's order is unchanged and the displayed rate is restored.
issues.overall_effect: the concluding rate extraction (T2_11)–(T2_3) and hence the stated O(N^{−2/(n+2)}log⁴N) bound of Theorem 1 are not established by the written estimates.
issues.title: Setting δ = ε leaves the additive 6δ deviation term above the claimed rate
issues.why_classification: a one-line re-optimization of the free parameter fixes the extraction with the same rate; no substantive content is lost.
